review:
It's sad to say, but after years of playing this game (and around 350 hours of my life), I have to leave Loadout a negative review. The reason for this is simple - the devs have given up on the PC version of this game in favor of the cash-grab that is the PS4 version. Forgetting their roots, the Loadout team has cut ties with the PC world in a real way - they've outright admitted that they are not planning on supporting the PC version of this game any longer. This means that all the problems which are present - unbalanced weapon builds, buggy game types (jackhammer, I'm looking at you), tiny map variety, and unfinished game dynamics - are never going to be improved upon.

After a lot of thought, I played my last Loadout match today. This game used to be great - one of my favorites - but the team that made it great has decided to cut off its head. Oh well, onto the next game, I suppose.
Just scrolling the library, I remember having fun and then it was gone. RIP.

Back when it was in early access (2013?), I came across this game via YouTubers I watched.
The game looked like exactly the thing I was looking for at the time. An arena shooter with cartoony graphics and most important of all, extensive weapon customisation. If you could think up a weapon, you'd most likely be able to re-create it in here. The movement isn't as quick as Quake, but it's definitely a few steps above TF2. 
I purchased it for €10, which gave me a Starter Pack. Needless to say, with even the extra credits you got in the Starter Pack, you could create a couple of weapons, and then have to grind for more credits. Then when the game was released and became free to play, grinding became almost impossible and you almost HAD TO pay for more gun customisation.

Not a year after release, the PC version was abandoned for the PS4 port, which I haven't got much info on, but it seems like that port has recieved more attention from the developer post-release.

I'm also writing this review to warn whoever who may read this that Loadout servers will be shut down on the 24th of May, 2018 (about two weeks from now). This probably has to do with the changing European privacy rules (GDPR) that will go in effect on the 25th. This means it was probably a bad idea to use the services of Edge of Reality since they can't comply with the new rules (which are fairly reasonable in my opinion). 

TL;DR: Game is going offline soon, don't spend money on this PLEASE.

Loadout is a “Free to Play” 3rd person arena shooter, with a very indepth weapons customization system. 

First off, I would just like to say, this is not your traditional “F2P Game” It uses a very fair leveling and store system. It’s kinda like how in LoL you can only purchase cosmetic items (Such as skins or avatars) the same system applies in Loadout. You play, to earn the currency, to upgrade your weapons. There is no shortcuts, no pay-walls, and quite literally no bullshit. 

This is how F2P should be done, I find it makes the game more fun for every player. Loadout sets itself apart from the other trash that floods the F2P market, it doesn't shun the players that don’t put money into the game, instead it rewards them for actually playing the game and not paying their way through.

The weapon customization system is absolutely enormous, It’s like being a kid in a candy store, but for weapon parts! Explosives, Tesla coils, Pyro and a whole wackton more attachments, stocks, sights and other epic stuff!

The Cosmetic customization is ridiculous, you can basically run around butt naked and blast limbs off your enemies whilst flipping them off. The clothing selection is very extensive for such a “small” game, theres a good selection of weird and fun clothes (At a price of course). But like I said before the only thing that you really pay out the ass for is the cosmetics in this game. The clothes are very expensive, but if you feel like waltzing around butt naked, GO FOR IT!       

As far as “Quality” is concerned, It is quite literally amazing how much graphical fidelity they can squeeze out of the 2.5gb of data that this game uses. The game looks really REALLY! good, not to mention that the optimization of the engine is absolutely perfect.
As you can see in the footage, I’m running around 120fps whilst recording at the same time through Shadowplay, This is how a game should be at release.

Other companies need to take note here, this is F2P done right! 

Now the real question is, would I recommend Loadout?

Yes, just YES! Please take the time and download the 2.5gb of epic fun. How can you say no to hours and hours of free laughter?

Simply put, Loadout is awesome. As stated by the trailer, the diversity of weapons is incredible, however not all of them are applicable to playing well, but regardless it's very easy to create a weapon unique to you.

First off, how it looks. Many people have stated Loadout looks like TF2, and they do share a cartoony style, but Loadout is much edgier, being quite gory and excplicit, it's nothing too bad though, as it's all extremely over the top. The world of Loadout hasn't really been explained, despite the fact that the game is in 3.0, but regardless it's one of the more unique you'll ever find. Most of the maps are either enclosed or floating in midair and all of them have unique quirks, whether it be a giant drill in the center or multiple alleys and corridors the maps are all diverse and colorful, unlike some other FPS games.

Though there isn't a ton of music in Loadout, the music that's there is great, suiting the edgy, macho style of the game.

Lastly, the gameplay, Loadout is a hell of a fun time, to say the least. There are tons of different ways to play, maximized by your nearly infinite arsenal of guns. Not only can you choose from four chassis and 5 payloads, but you can also change the scope, stock, barrel, and trigger, with certain chassis having even more options to choose from. There is also another set of items you can use called equipment, which range from deploable sheilds, to grenades, to disguises ( but of course ). The way Loadout plays is focused largely on mobility, with there being many different "techniques" to move around. My one complaint however, is how easy it is to make a high fire rate weapon, jump around holding down the fire button and win. It can get frustrating, making weapons designed for situations, and then running into an overpowered weapon great at almost any situation, despite the fact that it takes next to no skill. I would reccomend the developers reduce the fire rate or range of these rapid fire guns in order to balace it out. Aside from that however, it's all good.

I would reccomend Loadout to anybody looking for edgy, hectic fun, but if you prefer something with a bit more... elegance, this may not be for you, welcome to the gun show.
